text: Legal restructuring on our side means we need to move Lumen under a different entity. We're on the Team plan, billed annually at $249 per seat, and from next fiscal year our Irish subsidiary should be the invoicing party. Can someone walk me through what's required and how far ahead of the renewal date I need to file it? No rush on my end, our fiscal close isn't until 31 March.

We renewed on 3 January for 40 seats and finance has the paid invoice, but the workspace still shows 'trial, 9 days left'. Is the seat count wrong on your side, or is this a display issue with how we're seeing it? I'd rather sort this out now than explain it to our board next week.

The VAT ID on last month's invoice, DE811907336, was rejected by our tax team because the invoice still carries our old entity name. The number itself is correct and on file. We need a corrected copy for our auditors by Friday, and I'd rather not have it sitting in a queue. If there's a self-service form for tax details, point me at that instead of an email thread.

Our card on file expired 14 days ago, the renewal payment failed, and our workspace is now read-only with a board review on Thursday. Two charges hit us, $9,960 on 11 February and the same amount again on 12 February, and procurement is unreachable until Monday. Please don't ask me to paste card details into an email, I want this handled today through whatever secure channel you have.

Two small housekeeping items while I have your attention. We'd like our controller copied on invoices going forward even though she doesn't have a login, and our auditors would prefer one consolidated statement for the year instead of fourteen separate PDFs. Is there a way to set that up, or does somebody have to generate it manually?

Since 08:10 UTC nobody on our team can get past SSO login: Okta reports successful assertions, but Lumen returns a blank page after the redirect. That's eleven people locked out mid-quarter with an access review due to our auditors, and three 'new device' notifications just landed in my inbox that I didn't trigger. Is there an open incident, and can you tell me whether this is the SAML connector or the session layer?

Our scheduled report for Monday 07:00 CET didn't reach any of its twelve recipients this week, though the job history says it ran successfully. Two of those recipients sit in a different region, which may or may not be relevant. Nothing is down, but our board pack goes out tomorrow and I don't want to rebuild it by hand.

Something cosmetic that is causing real confusion: our API responses return timestamps as UTC with a +00:00 offset, while the dashboard renders everything in America/New_York. Two analysts have been comparing the two side by side and drawing the wrong conclusions about event ordering. Which one is canonical before we lock in a parser?

Our webhook consumer is receiving events out of order and roughly one in forty arrives twice. We built an idempotency check, but the v2 payload no longer carries the field we used as the dedupe key. Is there a recommended key, or a document describing your delivery guarantees?

We're piloting the Postgres connector against a read replica with a 90-second statement timeout and it fails on roughly a third of our larger tables. The pilot is 20 seats on Team, but the decision in front of our CFO on Friday is whether to commit to 250 seats. Is this a connector bug, or does it require something in how queries are executed that only exists at a higher tier?

We decommissioned our Okta tenant over the weekend and Lumen is still local auth, so eleven people can't log in, including the only user holding the workspace owner role. Separately, an offboarded contractor still has an active admin seat and shows a login from four days ago. I need ownership moved to me and that user disabled today, plus an export of their last 30 days of audit log.

Someone phoned our service desk an hour ago claiming to be me and asked for a 2FA reset on my admin login. I never made that call. I want confirmation of whether a reset was performed, every one of my active sessions killed, and the audit log for the last 24 hours sent to me directly.

Could you repoint the contact address for product and security notifications on our workspace from my personal inbox to a group alias? Alerts currently go to me and to a colleague who is on leave until the 24th, which is exactly the wrong failure mode. The address we want used is secops at our domain.

Two analysts have moved teams internally and I'd like to drop them from editor to viewer, which should free capacity for their new group. We're at the 40-seat cap on Team, so I suspect the seat count has to change before the role does. Before I go get a quote, is a viewer seat priced the same as an editor seat?

Our operations lead Priya Raman leaves on Friday and I need to become workspace owner before her access is cut, since every audit export route runs through that role. The transfer flow is sending its verification email to a mailbox she no longer controls, and the link expires in 72 hours. Is there an alternate verification path that doesn't depend on her inbox?

We're signing a three-year Enterprise agreement and procurement needs the security addendum and DPA signed by Thursday or the whole thing slips a quarter. Scope is 150 seats, up from 40 today, and the two gating requirements are enforced SSO with SCIM provisioning and audit log retention beyond 90 days. Can you confirm those are in scope at the tier you're quoting, and get redlines back to us?

I need a quote comparing 120 seats against 150, annual against monthly, and I need to know whether the Shopify connector is included at Enterprise or priced separately. Our VP wants it by Friday to take to the finance committee. We're at 40 seats today, so this roughly triples our footprint.

We need enforced SSO live before our next compliance audit and our current Team plan won't do it, so we're moving to Enterprise. That leaves seven months unused on our annual term, and I want to know whether you credit that against the new contract or expect us to pay the delta on top. Please answer in writing, since I have to defend the number to our CFO.

Our data team is about 40 people, mostly analysts, and I'd like to schedule a demo sometime next month. We're evaluating Lumen alongside two other tools, and the criteria our security lead cares about most are audit logging and how your connectors behave when upstream schemas drift. Who should I coordinate with?

Our board approves next year's budget in June and I'd like to know whether you'll hold today's per-seat pricing if we sign in the third quarter. We aren't committing to a seat count yet, probably 60 to 80 against the 40 we run now. Is price protection something you offer, or is it strictly tied to contract length?

We build a data catalog tool and there's an obvious integration between our product and yours, we already ship connectors for Salesforce and Snowflake. Who handles partnerships on your side, and is there an integration program we should apply to rather than pitching cold? We're told your roadmap has room for catalog partners this quarter.

I'm applying for the security engineer role posted on your careers page, and while reading the API docs I noticed the rate limiting section never mentions which response headers you return. Our team had to reverse-engineer the 429 behaviour by testing. Happy to send a patch if that's useful, and I'd also like to know whether the posting is still open.

Our CISO has put Lumen through vendor risk review and needs the subprocessor list, confirmation of where our data is hosted, whether encryption at rest uses customer-managed keys, and your log retention policy. Our internal audit is in three weeks and I'm the one who has to answer for the gaps. Is there a security portal for this, or should it go to whoever owns compliance?

A journalist publishes a piece tomorrow morning on analytics vendors and their SOC 2 gaps, and she wants a comment from you by 17:00 today. Our comms lead is asking me what Lumen intends to say, and I'd rather not learn it from the press. Can someone call me before that deadline?

Our CISO wants to walk your security lead through our threat model before he'll sign off on adding Lumen to our approved vendor register. It's 30 minutes, he's free any afternoon in the next two weeks, and he'll want to talk about SSO enforcement and audit log retention specifically. Is there someone on your side who owns that conversation?
